title: Near, Opposite, Far
label: ch:mr-near-opposite-far
canDo: I can place something near or in front of a landmark, say that it is far, and tell a postposition apart from an ordinary word by whether it bends the noun in front of it.

payoff.summary: Complete MR-R43-how-far and answer one where-question three ways -- near Pune, in front of the room, far -- naming which of the three needed no ending at all.
payoff.note: lāmb is in this chapter precisely because it is NOT a postposition: the contrast is what makes the oblique rule falsifiable rather than decorative.
